researched_by: the Authority's own car park byelaws (2018 and 2024 texts), its parking and camping pages, and Resources Committee papers on democracy.peakdistrict.gov.uk
policy_summary:
One of the cleanest and best-evidenced prohibitions in the dataset, and the only national park so far that closes its car parks by BYELAW rather than by signage or a parking order. The Authority runs 44 car parks with about 2,000 spaces, and every one of them is named in a schedule to byelaws made under section 90 of the National Parks and Access to the Countryside Act 1949.

Two byelaws do the work, and they are different offences. Byelaw 4 (headed OVERNIGHT PARKING in the 2024 text, LIMIT ON WAITING in the 2018 text) says no vehicle may be left on the land 'between the hours of 12 midnight and 6 a.m.' - a closure, applying to every vehicle, whether anyone is inside it or not. Byelaw 6 (byelaw 9 in 2018) is the camping clause: no tent, no vehicle 'including a caravan', no other structure, used 'for the purpose of camping/overnight sleeping'. Penalty for either is a fine not exceeding level 2 on the standard scale, currently GBP 500. The website puts it plainly: 'Overnight parking or camping at all of our car parks is prohibited, and may be subject to patrols and enforcement action.'

The change worth recording is small and deliberate. The 2018 byelaw ended 'for the purpose of camping.' The 2024 byelaw ends 'for the purpose of camping/overnight sleeping.' Those three words close the argument that sleeping in a van with the curtains shut is not camping. Everything else in the 2024 revision was administrative - tariffs and fine levels were stripped out of the byelaw text so charges can be changed without going back to the Secretary of State each time.

Enforcement is unusual and worth understanding. There is no PCN and no FPN: the Authority issues a Notice of Charge and Intention to Prosecute, and if it is not paid within 28 days it obtains keeper details from DVLA and takes the matter to the magistrates. A byelaw breach is a criminal matter, not a civil parking debt.

Provision exists but it is a campsite, not an aire. North Lees at Hathersage, which the Authority runs itself, opened five dedicated campervan bays with optional electric hook-up for the 2026 season. GBP 25 a night including one person, GBP 7 for hook-up. That is the only place in the Authority's ownership where you may lawfully sleep in a vehicle.
notes:
The direction of travel is tightening, and January 2026 shows exactly how. The Resources Committee approved a strategy for a NEW set of byelaws covering road verges on the North Lees Estate at Stanage - the classic overspill when the pay-and-display car parks fill or people decline to pay. The report says in terms that 'the proposed byelaws would also allow drivers of campervans parking overnight within passing places/laybys within Authority ownership or access land to be prosecuted in a similar manner.' Same level 2 fine, pursued through the Single Justice Procedure. This is the Authority closing the obvious loophole in its own car park byelaws: banned from the car park at midnight, you moved fifty metres onto the verge, and now that is being caught too.

The midnight-to-6am rule is the more interesting of the two byelaws for a van user, because it does not care what you are doing. Byelaw 6 requires you to be camping or sleeping. Byelaw 4 requires only that the vehicle is there. A van parked empty in Tideswell Dale at 1am is already in breach. That distinction matters when people reason that they will just sit up and not sleep.

Ownership is a trap here and the register is right to flag it. The two car parks most visitors associate with the Peak District honeypots - Castleton, and the main Edale car and coach park - are HIGH PEAK BOROUGH COUNCIL, not the Authority. Bakewell's town-centre car parks (Market Place, Granby Road, Hawkhill Road, Main Street, Nether End, Oddfellows Road) are Derbyshire Dales District Council. Fairholmes, Derwent and the reservoir car parks are Severn Trent, United Utilities and Yorkshire Water. The Authority's own Edale car park is Barber Booth, and its own Bakewell car parks are Bakewell Station on the Monsal Trail and Aldern House at its headquarters. Four separate regimes can apply within one valley.

The coordinates in this file are unusually solid: every Authority car park is listed with a six-figure OS grid reference in the schedule to the byelaws themselves, which is about as authoritative a source as a location can have. They were converted from OSGB36 to WGS84 rather than looked up.

One curiosity: the Authority states that none of its car parks have height barriers and that they are therefore 'suitable for small to medium sized motorhomes where spaces are available' - it will happily take a motorhome's money until midnight. The objection is to the night, not the vehicle.
open_questions: Confirmation date of the 2024 car park byelaws. They were sealed 28 May 2024 and objections closed 17 July 2024, after which the Authority applied to the Secretary of State. The confirmed text is published on the Authority's site as 'PDNPA Byelaws Car Parks 2024', which implies confirmation, but no confirmation date was found. It does not change the substance - the 2017/2018 byelaws they revoke contain the same midnight-6am and camping prohibitions.
Whether the North Lees verge byelaws have been advertised, consulted on and confirmed since the January 2026 committee decision. Recorded here as draft.
How hard byelaw 4 is actually enforced overnight. 'Patrols and enforcement action' is asserted, but no prosecution numbers were found, and a magistrates' court route is expensive to run at scale.
Whether the five North Lees campervan bays have a maximum stay. None is published.

Whether the Authority is negotiating with Derbyshire County Council to extend verge restrictions onto highway verges that are not access land - the January 2026 report says talks are under way but gives no outcome.

The published 2024 schedule shows Wyedale (Buxton) and White Lodge (Ashford) with what appears to be the same grid reference; one is likely a transcription error in the PDF. Neither is mapped here as a result.

Checked 2026-07-27 for Authority-run provision away from the parking pages, and the answer is no. North Lees is the only campsite the Peak District National Park Authority runs, and its five campervan bays with optional electric hook-up are already recorded. The Authority's camping page names nothing else - no camping barns, no bunkhouses, no hostels - and directs everything else to Visit Peak District's commercial guide. The only other Authority accommodation found is Cattiside Cottage, a two-bedroom self-catering cottage on the North Lees Estate, which is not vehicle provision.

The Peak District camping barn network was historically associated with the National Park. Nothing on the Authority's 2026 site mentions camping barns at all. Whether they were transferred to YHA or to the barn owners, and when, was not established - it would be worth knowing only because a barn with vehicle parking would be a stopping place.
North Lees now closes from the afternoon of 23 December 2026 until 4 January 2027; otherwise it is open all year. The existing campervan bay record does not carry that closure.
Does the Authority own or let any land on the Warslow Moors Estate that carries a camping or caravan operation? Nothing was found, but the estate was not searched systematically.

sites.notes: NEW FOR 2026 and the only place on Authority land where you may lawfully sleep in a vehicle. Five dedicated campervan bays with optional electric hook-up, run by the Authority itself on the Stanage-North Lees Estate. GBP 25 a night includes one person; further adults GBP 13, 13-17s GBP 10, 5-12s GBP 7, under-5s free, dogs GBP 4. Bank holiday Fri/Sat/Sun nights carry a GBP 2.50 per guest surcharge. Open year round apart from a Christmas closure. Roof tents are allowed in the campervan bays only. Prices quoted valid to 31 December 2026. A campsite pitch, not an aire - book ahead, no overnight arrivals.

sites.name: All Peak District National Park Authority car parks - midnight to 6am closure (byelaw 4)
sites.notes: Byelaw 4, headed OVERNIGHT PARKING in the 2024 text and LIMIT ON WAITING in the 2017/2018 text, in identical words: 'No person shall, without the consent of the Authority, leave any vehicle or cause or permit any vehicle to be left on the land between the hours of 12 midnight and 6 a.m.' Applies to all 44 scheduled Authority car parks and to every vehicle - occupied or not, sleeping or not. This is the clause that catches a van user who reasons that sitting up all night is not camping. Fine not exceeding level 2 on the standard scale (GBP 500). Enforced by Notice of Charge and Intention to Prosecute, then DVLA keeper lookup and magistrates' court, not by PCN or FPN. Note the asymmetry with the daytime tariff, which runs 9am to 6pm - the hours between 6pm and midnight are neither charged nor prohibited.

sites.name: All Peak District National Park Authority car parks - camping and overnight sleeping (byelaw 6)
sites.notes: Byelaw 6 of the 2024 byelaws (byelaw 9 of the 2017/2018 set): 'No person shall on the land, without the consent of the Authority, erect or use a tent or use any vehicle, including a caravan, or any other structure for the purpose of camping/overnight sleeping.' The words 'overnight sleeping' were ADDED in 2024 - the 2018 text stopped at 'camping'. A deliberate three-word tightening aimed squarely at people who argue that sleeping in a van is not camping. Fine not exceeding level 2 (GBP 500), pursued through the magistrates. A separate offence from byelaw 4, and both can bite on the same night.

sites.name: Wild camping on all land owned by the Peak District National Park Authority
sites.notes: The Authority's camping page is blunt: 'We do not allow wild camping on any land that we own', and 'There is no provision under the Countryside and Rights of Way Act for camping on open access land.' Camping anywhere in the park without the landowner's permission is a trespass. This covers Authority land beyond the car parks - the Stanage-North Lees Estate, trail land and open moorland - where no byelaw is in force but the landowner's position is unambiguous. Directed at tents, but applies with at least equal force to vehicles, which cannot lawfully be driven onto most of it anyway.

sites.name: Road verges, laybys and passing places, North Lees Estate and Stanage
sites.search_hint: North Lees Estate verges, Burbage Bridge to Callow Bank, Hollin Bank Road
sites.notes: APPROVED IN PRINCIPLE 23 JANUARY 2026, NOT YET IN FORCE. Resources Committee approved the strategy and delegated authority to advertise, consult and apply to the Secretary of State. Draft text: 'no person shall, except upon the direction or with the permission of a Police Officer or of an Enforcement Officer cause or permit any vehicle (and/or drawn Trailer) to Wait in the Prohibited Areas', with a schedule of road sections by grid reference - Burbage Bridge to Callow Bank, Callow Banks to Hooks Carr, Hooks Carr to Cattis Side, and parts of Hollin Bank Road. The committee report is explicit about vans: 'The proposed byelaws would also allow drivers of campervans parking overnight within passing places/laybys within Authority ownership or access land to be prosecuted in a similar manner.' Justified by SSSI damage, blocked access and litter when the pay-and-display car parks fill or drivers avoid the charge. Fine up to GBP 500 via the Single Justice Procedure. Exemptions for boarding and alighting, deliveries, emergency vehicles, maintenance and holders of an Authority waiver. Separate talks are under way with Derbyshire County Council about highway verges that are not access land. A linear zone rather than a point, so no coordinates.

sites.notes: The Authority's own Bakewell car park - NOT the town-centre ones, which are Derbyshire Dales District Council. Explicitly flagged by the Authority as 'not suitable for motorhomes' even by day, on space grounds. Byelaws 4 and 6 apply: no vehicle left midnight to 6am, no sleeping in a vehicle at any time. 25 spaces, 2 accessible.

sites.name: All other Peak District National Park Authority car parks
sites.notes: The Authority operates 44 car parks with roughly 2,000 spaces and all are named in the schedule to the byelaws, each with a six-figure grid reference. The ones not individually recorded here carry exactly the same regime: Alsop-en-le-Dale, Alstonefield, Aldern House, Blore Pastures, Brookside, Carr Lane (Thornhill), Clough House, Crowden, Dennis Knoll, Derbyshire Bridge, Derwent Overlook, Friden, Hartington Station, Hollin Bank, Hooks Carr, Hurdlow, Hurst Clough, Ilam Coach Lay-by, Mapleton Lane, Milldale, Minninglow, Moor Lane, Nab Quarry, Narlows Lane, Ravensdale, The Street, Thorpe Station, Tissington, Trentabank, Upper Burbage Bridge, Upperdale, Vicarage Quarry, Waterhouses, White Lodge, Wyedale. Two are free (The Street in the Goyt Valley, and Crowden); the rest are pay and display, 9am to 6pm, GBP 4.75 all day, GBP 40 for an annual permit. Ilam Coach Lay-by takes coaches and minibuses only - no cars, vans or motorhomes at any time. Fourteen sites allow late payment within 24 hours because of poor mobile signal, which is a payment concession and not permission to remain overnight.

provision_sweep_2026_07_27: Gap-filling sweep for provision the car park pages do not mention (research protocol step 2). Result: nothing new. The Authority runs exactly one campsite, North Lees, whose five campervan bays are already in this file. No camping barns, bunkhouses or hostels are run by the Authority in 2026, and the only other Authority accommodation is a self-catering cottage on the North Lees Estate. This is a genuine negative rather than an unsearched gap: the Authority's own camping page was read and lists nothing else.
